Should be using bmcweb utility function instead. See: https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/3132dacead062fa63c070fc7f404f8cf93df43a0/docs/COMMON_ERRORS.md#15-using-async_method_call-where-there-are-existing-helper-methods

Thanks. Changed to use dbus::utility::getAllProperties() as recommended.

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/86977/7/redfish-core/lib/processor_metrics.hpp#89
L106 prevents this function from being called if this interface doesn't exist for the objPath object. So should this be treated as an error here?

Thanks. Added messages::internalError() since this function is only called when interface exists (per L106 check), so D-Bus failure here indicates a real error.

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/86977/7/redfish-core/lib/processor_metrics.hpp#45
Should this be returning an error?

Thanks. Yes, added messages::internalError(). If getAllProperties succeeds but unpackPropertiesNoThrow fails, it indicates unexpected property type mismatch - this is a real error that should be reported.

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/86977/7/redfish-core/lib/processor_metrics.hpp#59
Should both of these be nlohmann::json::object_t?

Thanks.Removed the local variables entirely. Now using direct assignment to asyncResp->res.jsonValue["CacheMetricsTotal"]["LifeTime"]["..."] instead, which avoids the type question.

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/86977/7/redfish-core/lib/processor_metrics.hpp#65

Seems like it would be clearer to not use the local variable for the JSON object since this is a simple assignment.

i.e.
asyncResp->rec.jsonValue["CacheMetricsTotal"]["LifeTime"]["Corr...

(Same comment below for other use of lifeTime variable.

Not done.  "nullptr" means the properties didn't exist in teh response, and is arguably an internal error.  You need to handle when they're unavailable..

Thanks for remind. Changed to BMCWEB_LOG_ERROR and added messages::internalError when ceCount or ueCount is nullptr. Since both properties are always registered and updated together in dbus-sensors, nullptr here indicates an internal error rather than a normal unavailable case.

The xyz.openbmc_project.Memory.MemoryECC PDI definition does not include default properties for these two properties. I'm wondering if internalError here is too strict? Maybe it should be a WARNING instead?

Done. Removed messages::internalError() and changed BMCWEB_LOG_ERROR to BMCWEB_LOG_WARNING. Properties that are nullptr are now individually skipped instead of returning HTTP 500, matching the codebase pattern in systems.hpp for nullable D-Bus properties.

Done, thanks.

I think you can put those content before the `for` loop here,
so that the response would be initialized only after checking the existence of `processorId`
Done, thanks.

The ` @odata.id`, `Id`, `Name`, and the header are set here before `getProcessorObject` runs. 
If `processorId` doesn't exist, `getProcessorObject` -> `handleProcessorSubTree` calls `messages::resourceNotFound`, which merges the error into `jsonValue` without clearing these fields. The 404 response then carries a stale ` @odata.id`, ... alongside the error.

In this case, I think moving these content into the binded lambda would be better.
Done, thanks.
